points.why: It names shifting the burden and contrasts the symptomatic emergency response with the fundamental tree and cool-roof fix. It ties the erosion to the crew falling from 12 to 3 and to lost execution capacity.
It describes a self-reinforcing capacity loss ('couldn't spend it at the old rate', which makes the cuts look justified) and the 10–20 year lag before trees provide meaningful shade.

It keeps the emergency response funded through a dedicated reserve, bars reprogramming of prevention funds, and calls for deliberately rebuilding forestry staffing. It treats the centers as the symptomatic side of one portfolio.
It tracks canopy cover and prevention spending against emergency spending, but not crew size or planting rate as capability measures.

pitfalls.why: It correctly uses shifting the burden and never claims cooling centers worsen heat.
It does not propose cutting the cooling centers.
